title: Quesadillas
subtitle: Flour tortillas filled with melted cheese and griddled until crispy
excerpt: Quesadillas are flour tortillas filled with cheese and cooked on a dry griddle or frying pan until the cheese melts and the outside is crispy and golden. The most basic version is just cheese; they can be filled with cooked chicken, black beans, sweetcorn, or vegetables. Served with guacamole and soured cream.
sourceNotes: Quesadillas originated in colonial Mexico and are eaten throughout the country. In Mexico, a quesadilla traditionally uses a corn tortilla and requires only cheese (queso). The flour tortilla version with multiple fillings is particularly associated with northern Mexico and the Mexican-American border cuisine.

content.text: Cook quesadillas in a dry pan with no oil. The fat in the cheese lubricates the tortilla. Press down gently with a spatula for maximum contact between the tortilla and the pan, which produces a more evenly golden surface. Once the cheese melts, the quesadilla holds itself together when folded.

items.prepNote: grated, or mix of cheddar and mozzarella

content.text: Heat a dry frying pan over medium heat. Place a tortilla flat in the pan. Scatter half the cheese over one half of the tortilla. Add jalapeño and coriander if using. Fold the empty half over the filled half.

Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, pressing gently, until the underside is golden. Flip and cook for 2 more minutes until the second side is golden and the cheese is fully melted. Remove and cut into wedges. Keep warm while you cook the remaining quesadillas.

Add any of the following with the cheese: shredded cooked chicken, black beans (drained), sweetcorn, thinly sliced courgette, sautéed mushrooms, or leftover pulled pork. The filling should be pre-cooked; the quesadilla cooking time is too short to cook raw ingredients.
